```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
data.table::setDTthreads(2)
```

scphasedcn calls copy-number alterations in single cells from SPLONGGET data: single-cell long-read DNA sequencing in
which every read carries a 10x Multiome cell barcode and is sequenced on Oxford Nanopore. Per cell and region it
combines two channels:

- **depth**: fragments per region against an expected count from a reference (cells of the same cell type in normal
  tissue, a GC / mappability model in tumours), scored as a z against a Student-t null;
- **read-phased alleles**: every molecule that covers a phased heterozygous SNP votes for one haplotype; allelic
  imbalance is scored with beta-binomial likelihood ratios.

Two modes:

- **normal tissue** (`mode = "normal"`): rare, cell-private events. Thresholds come from null cells (cells the caller
  selects as copy-number neutral, or that you give), cross-validated at 1 false call per 1,000 null cell-regions; cells
  are also called in pools (random pools within a cell type, chromatin-kNN pools).
- **tumour** (`mode = "tumour"`): clones. The caller discovers clones, fits their allele-specific copy-number states,
  re-assigns every cell by likelihood and reports per-cell calls inherited from the clone or confirmed by the cell.

## The workflow

1. **Phase** heterozygous SNPs of the sample (e.g. Clair3 + longphase on the pooled BAM) and select them with
   `scphasedcn select-hets`. Normal tissue needs chromosome-scale haplotypes: orient the read-backed blocks with a
   population phase of the same sample (`scphasedcn hybrid-phase`); tumour mode uses the blocks as they are.
2. **Extract** with the Python package `scphasedcn` (`scphasedcn run`): per-cell 100 kb bin counts, a fragment table with
   the haplotype of every fragment, and per-cell QC.
3. **Call** with `call_scn()` in R, or the command-line script shipped with the package.

`vignette("scphasedcn-inputs")` describes steps 1 and 2, the input files and the cell metadata;
`vignette("scphasedcn-outputs")` the result tables.

## A run on simulated data

The package simulates SPLONGGET-like data and writes it in the layout the extractor produces. Here: 120 cells of
normal tissue (female) in three cell types, a few cells carrying private events (a chr1p loss, a chr8 gain), and one
phase block per chromosome (chromosome-scale phasing, as normal tissue needs).

```{r sim}
library(scphasedcn)
library(data.table)
ev = data.table(chrom = c("chr1", "chr8"), start = c(0, 0), end = c(24e6, NA),
                cnA = c(1L, 2L), cnB = c(0L, 1L), type = "private")
sim = simulate_scn(n_cells = 120, sex = "female", cell_types = c(epi = 0.4, fib = 0.35, imm = 0.25),
                   depth = c(meanlog = log(15000), sdlog = 0.3), events = ev, private_frac = 0.08,
                   multiplet_rate = 0, phase_block_mean = 1e9, switch_rate = 2e-6, seed = 7)
dir = file.path(tempdir(), "extract")
invisible(write_sim_dataset(sim, dir))
list.files(dir)
```

The simulated genome is small (chr1, chr2, chr8, chr21, chr22, chrX), so the run gets a centromere table for it; on
real hg38 data the default (`hg38_centromeres()`) applies.

```{r centromeres}
cen = sim$scn$bins[, .(cstart = 1, len = max(end)), by = chrom]
cen = cen[, .(chrom, cstart, cen_left = 0.4 * len, cen_right = 0.4 * len, cend = len)]
```

The cell types are in the simulated `cells_qc.tsv`; on real data they come from your own annotation through
`make_cell_meta()`.

```{r call, message = FALSE}
res = call_scn(dir, mode = "normal", sex = "female", centromeres = cen, null_cells = "select", verbose = FALSE)
res
```

Calls are per cell and region; `events` merges a cell's overlapping calls into events.

```{r events}
head(res$events[, .(cell, chrom, start, end, state, top_region, score)])
```

Compare with the truth of the simulation (the cells carrying the chr1p loss):

```{r truth}
carriers = colMeans(sim$truth$cn[sim$scn$bins$chrom == "chr1" & sim$scn$bins$end <= 24e6, ]) < 1.5
called = unique(res$events[chrom == "chr1" & state == "loss", cell])
table(carrier = sim$scn$cells$cell %in% sim$scn$cells$cell[carriers], called = sim$scn$cells$cell %in% called)
```

Write all tables, the parameters and the run notes:

```{r write}
out = file.path(tempdir(), "caller")
invisible(write_scphasedcn(res, out))
list.files(out)
scphasedcn_summary(res)
```

## From the command line

The package ships a command-line front end; its path is

```{r script}
system.file("scripts", "call_scn.R", package = "scphasedcn")
```

```bash
CALL=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", "call_scn.R", package = "scphasedcn"))')
Rscript $CALL --dir results/sample/extract --out results/sample/caller --sex female --mode normal \
    --cell-meta cell_meta.tsv --null-cells select
Rscript $CALL --dir results/tumour/extract --out results/tumour/caller --sex male --mode tumour \
    --events "20q_gain=chr20:28000000-;3p_loss=chr3:1-90000000"
Rscript $CALL --help
```

## Parameters

`caller_params()` reads the parameter file shipped with the package (`inst/config/caller.yaml`, one key per
`caller_defaults()` entry plus `normal:` / `tumour:` blocks). To change a value, copy the file, edit it and pass it
with `--caller-config` (or `caller_params(file = ...)` in R). Every run writes the values it used to `params.yaml`,
which reads back with `caller_params()`.

```{r params}
p = caller_params()
p[c("null_q", "eps", "mol_gap", "strata_breaks")]
```

The defaults were calibrated on SPLONGGET normal-tissue and tumour samples: the one-copy depth shifts (`shifts`) on
depth-only spike-ins into normal cells, `null_q` at 1 false call per 1,000 null cell-regions. The depth strata
(`strata_breaks`, clean fragments per cell) separate cells whose power differs; with much deeper or shallower data,
move them.

## Tumour mode

Tumour mode needs read-phased alleles (the allele votes drive the clone discovery). Phase blocks of longphase are not
oriented between blocks; the caller orients them per clone. Optional inputs: cells known to be normal (`flat` in the
cell metadata; the caller otherwise finds the normal clone itself), groups for the block orientation (`groups`, e.g.
spatial regions), known events (`events`, reported as their own regions) and multiplet probabilities
(`multiplets`).

```{r tumour, eval = FALSE}
res_t = call_scn("results/tumour/extract", mode = "tumour", sex = "male",
                 events = c(`20q_gain` = "chr20:28000000-"))
res_t$clones
head(res_t$segments)
```

MEDICC2 trees of the clones: `medicc2_pieces()` and `medicc2_table()` write MEDICC2's input from the clone
segments.
